Why The lakehouse is the AI program's foundation — literally: because the differentiated advantage has moved to the data layer and the operating model around it. The technology is the commodity; the discipline is the moat.

items: Unity Catalog-class governance makes AI corpora permission-safe by inheritance.
Cost governance from day one prevents the warehouse-bill surprise at month nine.
A data product registry turns governance into P&L, not committee minutes.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: We can describe exactly where The lakehouse is the AI program's foundation — literally programs stall, because we have inherited enough of them: contract-less integrations, drift without owners and dashboards nobody alerts on. The pattern exists to prevent precisely these.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Warehouse spend typically falls 25-40% under disciplined lakehouse migration.
Where this shows up in our work

This perspective is grounded in Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics and Enterprise BI & Executive Analytics within the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — each carried by our platforms with governance and evidence built in.
